title: Etale local module flatifications survive an earlier admissible blowup
statement:
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, $U\subset S$ a quasi-compact open, $f:X\to S$ a morphism of schemes, and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. Fix a finite family of commutative diagrams $e_i g_i=fj_i$ with $g_i:X_i\to S_i$, $e_i:S_i\to S$, and $j_i:X_i\to X$. Assume each $S_i$ is qcqs, $e_i$ is quasi-compact and etale, and $j_i$ is etale. Let $\mathcal J_i\subset\mathcal O_{S_i}$ be finite-type quasi-coherent ideals equal to the unit ideal on $e_i^{-1}U$ and suppose the strict transform of $j_i^*\mathcal F$ on $X_i\times_{S_i}\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J_i}S_i$ is flat over $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J_i}S_i$.

For any $U$-admissible blowup $b:S_1=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}S\to S$, put $U_1=b^{-1}U$, $X_1=X\times_SS_1$, $T_i=S_i\times_SS_1$, $Y_i=X_i\times_SS_1$, and let $\mathcal F_1$ be the strict transform of $\mathcal F$ for $\mathcal I$. The base $S_1$ and every $T_i$ are qcqs, $U_1$ is quasi-compact and $\mathcal F_1$ is quasi-coherent. The induced $T_i\to S_1$ are quasi-compact etale maps, and $Y_i\to X_1$ are etale maps; either family is jointly surjective whenever the corresponding original family is. With
$$T_i^*=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J_i\mathcal O_{T_i}}T_i,$$
the morphism $T_i^*\to T_i$ is admissible relative to the inverse image of $U_1$, and the module strict transform of $(Y_i\to X_1)^*\mathcal F_1$ is flat over $T_i^*$. There are canonical identifications
$$T_i\cong\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_{S_i}}S_i,\qquad T_i^*\cong\operatorname{Bl}_{(\mathcal I\mathcal O_{S_i})\mathcal J_i}S_i,$$
under which this final module is the successive strict transform obtained by first blowing up $\mathcal J_i$ and then the extension of $\mathcal I$. The identifications commute with the quotient maps from the ordinary pullback of $j_i^*\mathcal F$; the composite centre has zero set $V(\mathcal I\mathcal O_{S_i})\cup V(\mathcal J_i)$. Schemes, qcqs conventions, quasi-coherence, relative module flatness, admissible blowups, module strict transforms, fibre products and module pullbacks are as in [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [pqf-def-coherent], [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over], [def-nagata-admissible-blowup], [def-trf-module-strict-transform], [def-pc-fibre-product] and [def-pc-module-pullback]. Etale morphisms are as in [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Blowups themselves are those of [def-nagata-global-blowup].

source.place: Tag 0814, lemma-flatten-module-etale-localize, proof paragraph 1: preservation of the hypotheses under an admissible blowup and comparison of the two blowup orders. Returned proof steps 2 and 3.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-module-admissible-blowup-calculus] (2) to $b$: $S_1$ is qcqs and $\mathcal F_1$ is quasi-coherent. By [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open], $U_1\to U$ is an isomorphism, so $U_1$ is quasi-compact. This uses no quasi-compactness or finiteness assumption on $X$ or $\mathcal F$.

Write $A_i=\mathcal I\mathcal O_{S_i}$, $B_i=\mathcal J_i$, and $W_i=e_i^{-1}U$. Quasi-compactness of $e_i$ makes $W_i$ quasi-compact. Etale maps are flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Thus [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change], with the comparison of [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map], identifies $T_i=S_i\times_SS_1$ with $\operatorname{Bl}_{A_i}S_i$. The ideal $A_i$ is finite type and quasi-coherent and is the unit ideal on $W_i$: on affine inverse-image charts extension sends a finite generating list to its images and commutes with localization, by [def-nagata-extended-ideal] and [pqf-def-coherent]. Hence this is a $W_i$-admissible blowup, and [lem-trf-module-admissible-blowup-calculus] (2), applied over $S_i$, makes $T_i$ qcqs.

The maps $T_i\to S_1$ are base changes of $e_i$, and, by the fibre-product universal property, $Y_i\cong X_i\times_X X_1$ over $X_1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] to $e_i$ and $j_i$, and [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change] to $e_i$. They give the asserted etaleness and quasi-compactness. Whenever an original family covers, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change] gives joint surjectivity of that base-changed family. No covering hypothesis is needed for any other conclusion.

source.place: Tag 0814, lemma-flatten-module-etale-localize, proof paragraph 1: conditions (1) and (2).

proof.text: Let $d_i:T_i\to S_i$ be the projection. The inverse image $d_i^{-1}W_i$ equals the inverse image of $U_1$ under $T_i\to S_1$, by commutativity. It is quasi-compact because $T_i\to S_1$ is quasi-compact. The extended ideal $B_i\mathcal O_{T_i}$ is finite type and quasi-coherent: on affine charts it is generated by the images of generators of $B_i$, and these descriptions localize. It is the unit ideal on $d_i^{-1}W_i$. Thus its specified blowup $T_i^*\to T_i$ is admissible for this open, by [def-nagata-admissible-blowup]. Also $A_iB_i$ is finite type quasi-coherent: pairwise products of finite local generating lists generate it and localize; the product is the unit ideal on $W_i$.

Apply [thm-nagata-blowup-product-ideal] with its construction [def-nagata-blowup-product-comparison] over $S_i$, first to $(A_i,B_i)$ and then to $(B_i,A_i)$. Commutativity $A_iB_i=B_iA_i$ gives canonical identifications of $T_i^*$ with $\operatorname{Bl}_{A_iB_i}S_i$ and with the blowup of $S_i^*=\operatorname{Bl}_{B_i}S_i$ in $A_i\mathcal O_{S_i^*}$. The required composite-centre supports hold in both orders. Indeed $V(A_iB_i)=V(A_i)\cup V(B_i)$ by the prime-ideal criterion for a product. Moreover $V(B_i\mathcal O_{T_i})=d_i^{-1}V(B_i)$, so its image is contained in $V(B_i)$. Every point of $V(B_i)\setminus V(A_i)$ has a unique lift in this zero set, since $d_i$ is an isomorphism off $V(A_i)$ by [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement]. Therefore $V(A_i)\cup d_i(V(B_i\mathcal O_{T_i}))=V(A_iB_i)$. Interchanging $A_i,B_i$ proves the other support equality.

Put $H_i=j_i^*\mathcal F$, which is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]. Apply [lem-trf-module-strict-transform-flat-pullback] to $(f,e_i,g_i,j_i,\mathcal I,\mathcal F)$: both $e_i$ and $j_i$ are flat by their etaleness. It identifies $(Y_i\to X_1)^*\mathcal F_1$ with the $A_i$-strict transform of $H_i$ on $Y_i=X_i\times_{S_i}T_i$, commuting with the quotient maps from ordinary pullback. All identifications of these ambient fibre products are the projection-preserving ones from [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Tag 0814, lemma-flatten-module-etale-localize, proof paragraph 1; flat pullback of the defining supported-section quotient.

proof.text: We compare module transforms, not just scheme transforms. Apply [lem-trf-strict-transform-comparison-epimorphism] over $S_i$ to the first blowup $d_i$ and the second blowup in $B_i\mathcal O_{T_i}$, with specified composite ideal $K=A_iB_i$. Step 5 verifies precisely its centre-support hypothesis. It gives an epimorphism $\theta:N\twoheadrightarrow G$, where $N$ is the successive transform of $H_i$ and $G$ its $K$-strict transform, with $\theta\alpha=\beta$ for their quotient maps from ordinary pullback; its kernel is supported on the inverse image of $V(K)$. By [lem-trf-iterated-transform-exceptional-support], $N$ has no nonzero local sections supported there, using the support equality in that node. Consequently every section of $\ker\theta$ is zero, so $\theta$ is an isomorphism. Repeat these same two cited statements for the order $(B_i,A_i)$, with $K=B_iA_i$ and the second support equality of step 5. Both successive transforms are thus canonically $G$, and their comparison commutes with the ordinary-pullback quotient maps because each isomorphism satisfies $\theta\alpha=\beta$. Together with step 6, this identifies the module asked for in the item with the successive transform in the reverse order.

source.place: Tag 080I, lemma-strict-transform-composition-blowups (1); its proof comparing the quotient maps and supported kernels.

proof.text: By hypothesis, the first transform $H_i^{B_i}$ in the reverse order is flat over $S_i^*$. This base is qcqs by [lem-trf-module-admissible-blowup-calculus] (2), and the inverse image of $W_i$ is quasi-compact by [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open]. The second centre $A_i\mathcal O_{S_i^*}$ is finite type quasi-coherent and unit on that open, by the same local-generator argument as step 4. Apply [lem-trf-module-admissible-blowup-calculus] (2) to this second admissible blowup and $H_i^{B_i}$. Its strict transform is its ordinary pullback and is flat over $T_i^*$. Step 7 gives the required flatness in the original order. The asserted identification respects the quotient maps throughout, as established in steps 6 and 7; the centre zero set was computed in step 5.

Steps 1-2: calculus (2) and admissible-over-open give qcqs of S_1, quasi-coherence of F_1 and quasi-compactness of U_1. Flat base change (thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change) gives T_i≅Bl_{IO}S_i, and T_i is qcqs by calculus (2) over S_i. Step 3: the étale, quasi-compact and covering base-change lemmas apply, and joint surjectivity is claimed only when the original family covers. Step 4 (marked elementary) checks admissibility on d_i^{-1}W_i; that open is quasi-compact because T_i→S_1 is quasi-compact, and T_i is qs. Step 5: thm-nagata-blowup-product-ideal identifies both blowup orders with Bl_{A_iB_i}. The support equality V(A)∪d(V(BO))=V(AB) is proved correctly using the complement isomorphism.
